A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 20-page LRM/LPO study, including readable Appendices A–C. Extracted text and rendered pages match on pages 2–20; first-page differences concern resource availability, line wrapping, and the arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original diffusion-model evaluations and ablations in Section 5, plus a 200-prompt human study and additional reward-model experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, human evaluation, and additional experiments in Section 5 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same LRM architecture, VFE module, MPCF filtering, LPO objective, latent-space sampling procedure, and dynamic threshold.

E1.justification: Coverage is identical: Pick-a-Pic training/evaluation, GenEval and T2I-CompBench++ benchmarks, and human-study prompts from HPSv2 and DPG-Bench.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain identical comparator sets, including DDPO, D3PO, Diffusion-DPO, MaPO, and SPO where originally reported. Appendix B's reward-model comparator set is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendices A–B retain the same data splits, model configurations, metrics, 20-step DDIM procedures, training budgets, and human-study design.

E4.justification: The filtering, VFE, timestep-range, regularization, and threshold ablations are identical. Reward-model analyses and qualitative studies in Appendices B–C are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point estimates and human-study vote percentages. There are no changes to reported seeds, repeated runs, uncertainty estimates, or significance testing.

E6.justification: All benchmark scores, training-time comparisons, ablations, human-study outcomes, and qualitative results match. For example, Table 2 retains LPO PickScores of 21.69 for SD1.5 and 22.86 for SDXL.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(15), preference-consistency assumptions, and mathematical definitions of the objectives and threshold strategies are identical. No proofs or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The claims about noise-aware latent reward modeling, preference-alignment improvements, and 2.5–28× training speedup are retained. The abstract's scientific wording changes only through line wrapping.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are identical, including explanations of timestep effects and latent-space compatibility, and the stated restrictions to UNet-based models and DDPM scheduling.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a future code-release promise at casiatao/LPO with reported availability of code and models at Kwai-Kolors/LPO. This updates resource-access information; implementation details and Appendix A remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work, cited works, and novelty positioning are identical, including the claim of first employing diffusion models themselves for reward modeling.

P1.justification: Editing is limited to the abstract's resource-availability sentence and the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose, terminology, and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised availability sentence causes limited reflow within the first-page abstract, and the margin stamp changes. All figures, tables, and the layouts of pages 2–20 render identically.

improvement.justification: v2 replaces v1's future code-release promise with a code-and-model availability statement and an updated repository location. This modestly improves documented reproducibility and access guidance; the scientific evidence and appendices are unchanged. Actual repository contents cannot be established from the PDFs.
